title: BLUF
content: BLUF, short for bottom line up front, is a writing practice that puts the main point or the answer in the opening sentence of a passage.

meta.why: A reader who stops after one sentence still gets the answer, and the supporting detail follows for those who need it.
meta.example: A section on refund timing opens by stating that refunds post within five business days, then explains the exceptions.
meta.check: Read the opening sentence under each heading and confirm it answers the question the heading raises.
meta.limitation: Agencies recommend the practice for AI search, and platform documentation does not list it as a requirement.
meta.sources: Animalz: AEO glossary | https://animalz.co/blog/aeo-glossary | Industry glossary
